source: Canonical legacy identities 76-100 in data/v2-audit/current-question-audit.json order.

expansion_backlog_changes.core_trait_gap: non-virtue relational maintenance and mutual support
expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: maintaining mutual support and relational continuity vs. greater independence or redirected effort
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Legacy Yellow items frequently claim kindness, consideration, reliability, or organization instead of exposing the relational motive and a reasonable alternative.

expansion_backlog_changes.core_trait_gap: freedom and variety without distractibility or boredom confounds
expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: fresh possibility and freedom vs. sustained result, continuity, or predictable structure
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Batch 04 contains several Blue items that measure boredom, attention persistence, or inability to tolerate structure rather than a positive preference for possibility and freedom.

current.prompt: I work best when I can switch things up instead of doing the same task for long periods.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: task variety vs. sustained attention
measurement.what_it_measures: Preference for switching tasks rather than sustaining one task for a long period.

questions.why: Task switching can reflect role demands, attention regulation, or work design and is not independently Blue; stronger freshness items already cover the governed motive.

current.prompt: I connect most with people who are open, expressive, and genuine.

proposed.prompt: I tend to feel connected more quickly with people who share their thoughts and reactions openly than with people who reveal themselves gradually.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: open expressive immediacy vs. gradual relational disclosure
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether expressive openness in others accelerates a sense of connection.

questions.why: The revision removes ‘genuine’ as a virtue and measures a valid Blue preference in others against slower, equally legitimate disclosure.

current.prompt: I tend to resist schedules that feel overly rigid or restrictive.

proposed.prompt: Even when a schedule is practical, I prefer leaving some time uncommitted so I can follow an interesting possibility that emerges.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: room for emerging possibility vs. fully committed schedule
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether preserving uncommitted time for emerging possibilities feels preferable to a fully allocated schedule.

questions.why: The legacy words rigid and restrictive make resistance obvious; the revision gives a practical schedule credit while exposing the Blue freedom motive.

current.prompt: I feel most at ease when I know what the future is likely to look like.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: future predictability vs. openness
measurement.what_it_measures: Comfort from knowing what the future will probably look like.

questions.why: Ease about the future is vulnerable to anxiety and life-circumstance confounds and substantially overlaps stronger planning and predictable-progress items.

current.prompt: I get uneasy when expectations aren’t clearly defined.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: defined expectations vs. ambiguity
measurement.what_it_measures: Emotional discomfort caused by unclear expectations.

questions.why: The item measures unease and duplicates the stronger Batch 03 constraints-before-entry revision.

current.prompt: My natural communication style is…

proposed.prompt: You need to explain a complicated update to people who will use it differently. What do you establish first?

options.label: The decision or result they need to act on
An engaging exchange that helps possibilities surface
A sense of trust and how the change affects the people involved
The evidence, definitions, and logic that make the update clear

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: actionable result vs. engaging exchange vs. trust and impact vs. evidence and logic
measurement.what_it_measures: Which foundation someone establishes first when communicating a complicated update.

questions.why: The legacy item lists color stereotypes; the revision uses one situation and four competent, motivation-centered communication priorities.

current.prompt: I push through distractions when there’s a clear goal at stake.

proposed.prompt: When a goal is ambitious but reachable, competing against a clear standard brings out my best effort.

replacement.prompt: When a goal is ambitious but reachable, competing against a clear standard brings out my best effort.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: effort toward a demanding standard vs. less outcome-defined motivation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether a clear, ambitious standard naturally increases effort.

questions.why: Pushing through distraction is a competence claim; the candidate measures the governed Red achievement motive without implying superior self-control.

current.prompt: I struggle to stay motivated when everything feels too structured.

proposed.prompt: I feel more energized by a project when I can shape it as new possibilities emerge than when the path is fixed from the start.

replacement.prompt: I feel more energized by a project when I can shape it as new possibilities emerge than when the path is fixed from the start.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: emergent possibility vs. fixed path
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether shaping a path as possibilities emerge feels more energizing than following a fixed path.

questions.why: The legacy item asks respondents to admit poor motivation; the candidate compares two workable project structures.

current.prompt: I feel responsible for keeping things moving when others hesitate.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: moving a group forward vs. continued consultation
measurement.what_it_measures: Taking responsibility for momentum when others hesitate.

questions.why: This repeats the same semantic family as Question 28 and C01-L-R-01, already proposed as its stronger replacement.

current.prompt: I prefer events or activities that feel productive rather than just passing time.

proposed.prompt: After an open afternoon, I feel more satisfied when I can point to something I completed than when I simply enjoyed how the time unfolded.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: completed result vs. enjoyment of unstructured time
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether visible completion provides more satisfaction than an enjoyable unstructured afternoon.

questions.why: The legacy productive-versus-passing-time wording moralizes leisure; the revision gives both uses of time legitimate value.

current.prompt: I feel more comfortable trusting people once they’ve proven they’re reliable.

proposed.prompt: Before relying on someone for an important commitment, I prefer seeing consistent follow-through over time rather than trusting an encouraging first impression.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: evidence from follow-through vs. initial relational impression
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether demonstrated consistency is preferred to an encouraging first impression before reliance.

questions.why: The revision anchors Green in evidence and repeatability rather than claiming that cautious trust itself is Green.

current.prompt: I feel most alive when I’m laughing, talking, or sharing experiences with others.

proposed.prompt: I feel more energized by social time with lively interaction and varied conversations than by one quiet, sustained conversation.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: lively varied interaction vs. quiet sustained conversation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether lively interaction and conversational breadth are more energizing than quiet depth.

questions.why: The legacy item compounds laughter, talking, sharing, and aliveness; the revision isolates Blue social energy against a valid alternative.

current.prompt: I’m motivated by achieving visible results and tangible rewards.

proposed.prompt: I’m motivated by achieving visible results and tangible rewards.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: visible outcome motivation vs. process, experience, or relational motivation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether visible results and tangible rewards naturally motivate effort.

questions.why: The item directly names two historically established Red motivations without relying on directness, confidence, or generic competence.

current.prompt: I often put effort into keeping relationships balanced and supportive.

proposed.prompt: In an important relationship, I prefer making ongoing adjustments that keep support mutual rather than expecting each person to manage their needs independently.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: ongoing mutual support vs. independent need management
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether mutual relational support is preferred to greater independence within a relationship.

questions.why: The revision replaces a generic claim of supportive effort with two legitimate relationship models and an explicit Yellow continuity preference.

current.prompt: I get bored doing the same things the same way for too long.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: variety vs. repetition
measurement.what_it_measures: Boredom caused by repeated activity performed in the same way.

questions.why: Boredom tolerance is ambiguous and this duplicates the governed freshness-versus-working-routine family already retained through C02-L-B-02.

current.prompt: I lose interest quickly if something stops feeling engaging.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: continued engagement vs. changing interest
measurement.what_it_measures: Speed of losing interest when an activity becomes less engaging.

questions.why: The statement measures attention persistence or self-control and asks respondents to admit a weakness rather than a governed Blue preference.

current.prompt: I’m more productive when I enjoy the process, not just the outcome.

proposed.prompt: An engaging process keeps me involved more naturally than the promise of a strong outcome by itself.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: engaging process vs. outcome-only motivation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether ongoing engagement is more motivating than the promised outcome alone.

questions.why: The revision removes productivity as a competence claim and preserves a clean Blue-versus-Red motivational distinction.

current.prompt: I enjoy stepping outside my comfort zone just to see what happens.

proposed.prompt: I’m drawn to trying something unfamiliar when the main reward is discovering what the experience might open up.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: discovery through experience vs. known purpose or preparation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether discovery itself makes an unfamiliar experience attractive.

questions.why: Stepping outside a comfort zone can sound courageous or virtuous; the revision makes Blue discovery the sole reason for trying the unfamiliar.

current.prompt: Trying something new feels exciting rather than stressful to me.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: excitement vs. stress
measurement.what_it_measures: Emotional reaction to trying something new.

questions.why: The item confounds Blue novelty with anxiety and substantially duplicates the stronger unpredictable-new-experience item retained as Question 71.

current.prompt: I’m more relaxed socially when there’s a schedule or structure to the event.

proposed.prompt: At a social event, I prefer knowing the basic plan and timing rather than letting the gathering unfold without a defined shape.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: known plan and timing vs. open-ended unfolding
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether a defined social-event structure feels preferable to an open-ended gathering.

questions.why: The revision removes social anxiety and measures Green structure in a legitimate non-work context.

current.prompt: I feel most comfortable when outcomes are predictable.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: predictability vs. uncertainty
measurement.what_it_measures: Comfort from predictable outcomes.

questions.why: The item is vulnerable to anxiety and context effects and duplicates several stronger Green tradeoff items already proposed.

current.prompt: Trust builds slowly for me, but once it’s there, it’s solid.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: gradual trust vs. rapid connection
measurement.what_it_measures: Slow development and later durability of trust.

questions.why: The statement is closer to Yellow loyalty than Green, but also confounds relational history and introversion and overlaps the approved depth-versus-breadth candidate.

current.prompt: I don’t mind taking charge of plans if it keeps things moving.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: taking charge for momentum vs. waiting for shared direction
measurement.what_it_measures: Willingness to take charge to preserve momentum.

questions.why: The semantic family is already represented more clearly by C01-L-R-01; retaining another paraphrase would add redundancy rather than coverage.

current.prompt: If I want to improve, I…

options.wording: set a hard goal and push
change my environment to stay motivated
get accountability from someone I trust
build a system and track it

proposed.prompt: A personal goal has stopped improving despite steady effort. Which response would you most naturally try next?

options.label: Raise or sharpen the target and recommit to the result
Change the approach or setting to create fresh energy and possibilities
Involve someone I trust and create dependable shared accountability
Examine the pattern and build a repeatable way to track what changes

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: sharper result vs. fresh possibility vs. trusted accountability vs. evidence and tracking
measurement.what_it_measures: Which motivation guides recovery when improvement has stalled despite effort.

questions.why: The revision makes all four responses useful recovery strategies and removes compound stereotypes and superior-competence implications.

current.prompt: I think organization is important because it affects more than just me.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: organized consideration vs. personal autonomy
measurement.what_it_measures: Belief that personal organization matters because it affects others.

questions.why: The item rewards organization and consideration as virtues while neither independently establishes Yellow.
